results.name: H1-1_clean_detector_only_table
results.intended_semantic_state: no synthesis occurred; all cells detector-original
results.note: baseline: confirms the metric reads 0 when there is nothing to find

results.name: H1-2_single_synthesized_cell_pokes_above
results.intended_semantic_state: exactly one synthesized cell violates containment by exactly 5px
results.expected: undershoot == 5.0 (not more, not less -- proportional to the poke)
results.note: tests PROPORTIONALITY: the metric should scale with actual poke distance, not just flag binary presence

results.name: H1-3_detector_native_cell_pokes_no_synthesis_marker
results.intended_semantic_state: a cell with NO synthesis marker still violates containment
results.expected: undershoot == 5.0 -- the GEOMETRIC test cannot see the confidence marker, by design; this is what makes the empirical 0/1867 finding meaningful evidence rather than a tautology (the check COULD have flagged non-synthesized cells, and empirically never did)
results.note: CRITICAL: proves the undershoot metric is not somehow only capable of detecting synthesized cells by construction -- the 0/1867 empirical finding is real evidence, not a measurement artifact

results.name: H1-4_stamp_label_present_geometry_clean
results.intended_semantic_state: document carries stamp/occlusion labels but geometry is perfectly clean
results.expected: undershoot == 0 despite the label -- the metric must be purely geometric and must NOT special-case documents by label
results.note: confirms the evaluator has no hidden label-conditioned logic that would make H1's correlational finding circular

results.name: H1-5_severity_direction_stamp_vs_nonstamp
results.intended_semantic_state: a 'stamp-labeled' table with an 8px poke vs a 'non-stamp' table with a 150px poke
results.expected: the metric reports nonstamp_undershoot (150-100=150... let's just check it's larger) > stamp_undershoot regardless of label -- reproducing h1_resolution.json's empirical severity-direction finding in miniature
results.note: directly instantiates the counterintuitive empirical result: severity is NOT gated by the stamp/occlusion label in the measurement itself, consistent with 029/030 finding label correlates with RATE not MAGNITUDE

results.name: H2-1_escape_far_from_neighbor_no_contamination
results.intended_semantic_state: escaping cell pokes 5px out of its own table, neighbor table is 100px away

results.name: H2-2_constructed_cross_table_contamination
results.intended_semantic_state: DELIBERATELY constructed case where an escaping cell's poke lands inside an adjacent table's bbox -- this is the exact adversarial scenario H2 predicts is geometrically impossible for REAL escapes (bounded by token size) but which is trivially constructible synthetically
results.expected: intersection IS detected (the evaluator correctly identifies contamination when it is deliberately present) -- this does NOT falsify H2 empirically (no real instance was found in the corpus) but PROVES the evaluator would have caught it if one existed
results.note: CRITICAL evaluator-validity check: if this case had come back False, H2's '0 contaminated cells found' result would be worthless (the checker might be broken, not the phenomenon absent). This proves the checker works.

results.name: H2-3_boundary_touching_not_crossing
results.intended_semantic_state: a cell bbox whose edge exactly TOUCHES (y1==100) the neighbor's edge (y0==100) without crossing into it
results.expected: no intersection (strict inequality semantics: touching is not overlapping)
results.note: tests the strict-vs-inclusive boundary convention in the intersects() predicate used to declare H2 unfalsified -- a wrong convention here could hide or fabricate a contamination result

results.name: H2-4_escape_magnitude_near_proxy_bound
results.intended_semantic_state: two synthetic escapes straddling the 40px 'typical token height' proxy bound h2_resolution.json used as a sanity check
results.expected: the metric correctly distinguishes 39px (under) from 41px (over) -- confirms the bound-check arithmetic itself is correct, independent of whether any REAL escape in the corpus approaches it (max real escape was 14.43px, well under)
results.note: arithmetic sanity check on the proxy-bound comparison used in h2_resolution.json

results.name: H2-5_per_cell_not_per_table_aggregation
results.intended_semantic_state: one table has TWO escaping cells: one clean (no contamination), one dirty (contaminates tbI) -- a per-TABLE boolean flag would need to catch the dirty one even though the clean one is fine
results.expected: clean_escape does not intersect tbI; dirty_escape DOES intersect tbI -- both must be evaluated independently
results.note: confirms h2_resolution.py's per-CELL (not per-table) evaluation loop is the correct granularity -- a coarser check could have missed a single contaminated cell among several clean ones in the same table
